chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Dirraj and Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about old wine that is made into vinegar, he said, 'There is no harm with it.'

key_terms.الْخَمْرُ: Wine (specifically the drink, often considered impure)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it (permissible/pure)

ai.seo_question: Is old wine that has turned into vinegar considered pure and permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that 'old wine' (*khamr 'atiqah*) which has naturally transformed into vinegar is permissible (*halal*) and pure (*tahir*). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the transformation (*istihlak*) of a substance into a new form removes its previous impurity, distinguishing it from wine that merely retains its alcoholic nature.
